nodes.title: kon/place measure: her number is graded only on a placed protractor. An off placement (vertex-off, centre-on-arm, any other) plays out the placement only (ring on O and the dashed join to her centre where the level names the mix-up); her number's chip stays neutral and no arm is drawn from her misplaced centre (it ran beside OB and confirmed a right 150). draw keeps her own arm from O and the angle it makes. Reverse if: children cannot tell from the ring and join alone that the placement is what to fix (then a placement cue that names no reading).

kon/place scale lettering (supersedes the 'inner first' omission of dc-r8-kon-scale-lettering): a clashing number slides along its own tick (inner inward up to 22 px, never onto the turning handle; outer outward up to 4 px); only where no slide parts a pair are both numbers at that tick left out together (never 0/90/180, never one scale alone). Numbers are drawn last on a ground halo, over every line. Letters A/B/O keep 4 px clear of every protractor line, arm, arc, dot, chip and number, O on the side away from the opening. At 360 fade 1 a turned protractor still leaves out one or two pairs on most turns. Reverse if: children misread where a pair is left out (then a magnified scale or a larger board on phones, never a font under the floor).

kon/place: four one-board-px position nudges (← ↑ ↓ →) beside the turn arrows, the law's own move act (no snap, no reading, no cue). Reverse if: a phone trial shows children use them to search for the placement by trial (then a slower step or fewer presses).
